newsitem.title: UK: Dry weather helps LIFFE wheat firm, but off highs.
newsitem.headline: Dry weather helps LIFFE wheat firm, but off highs.

text.p: LIFFE wheat firmed in active trade on Thursday, with concerns over the lack of moisture still driving the new crop up, although it ended off highs.
November was again the most active month on wheat, with 695 of a total 1,043 lots traded. It last changed hands 0.40 stg up at 100.25 stg, having seen a high of 100.75 stg.
"It was obviously overdone at 100.75," one trader said. "It seems to be running into resistance at 101.00," he said. "There are quite a few sellers at 100.50 and over."
Market sentiment is being driven by ideas the continued dry weather in the UK and other parts of Europe could limit new crop production, traders said.

New official figures showing an increase in the availability of wheat for export, released by the Home Grown Cereals Authority on Wednesday, did have a bearish impact, but it was limited, traders said.
"It shouldn't make much difference," the trader said.
Lackluster bidding and results in Thursday's EU grains tender also had little effect, he said.
He reckoned the dry weather would keep the market strong. "I think there's more potential on the upside, without a doubt," he said.
Sterling's continued high level had played little part in Thursday's trading, but a fall could help renew the impetus behind wheat futures. "If the pound weakens it could take off," he said.
Just 9 lots of barley were traded, with 7 on May, which last traded 1.00 stg up at 92.50 stg, its high of the day.
